🧊🧬 DARPA seeks to conquer extreme cold as Arctic arms race goes biological

The US is positioning itself for a long-term contest over one of the planet’s most valuable regions, poking into yet another frontier in search of an Arctic advantage.

👉 In the Pentagon’s research ecosystem, even ice is no longer just a natural constraint but something to be engineered and controlled. That is the logic driving DARPA’s Ice Control for Cold Environments (ICE) program.

The program is now entering its third phase, moving research from the first two stages toward testing and advanced development.

🪖 The goal is blunt: make extreme cold less capable of disrupting US military operations. DARPA is pursuing biologically sourced and bioinspired molecules that can control ice crystallization, growth and adhesion, turning nature’s survival mechanisms into tools that keep military systems operating.

And that is where the bigger picture comes in. The Arctic is not just a frozen wilderness. It sits on vast energy reserves, emerging shipping routes and increasingly important strategic corridors used by other world powers. 

➡️ As sea ice retreats, the Northern Sea Route and other potential passages are shortening Asia-Europe transit times by thousands of kilometers, while estimates of Arctic oil, gas and critical minerals continue to grow. The US is not waiting for nature to clear the way. Through programs such as DARPA’s ICE, it is developing ways to overcome the physical barriers that could limit its reach.

📑 Who is behind the project?

🔴 Michigan Technological University – a public research university specializing in engineering, cold-region science and environmental technologies

🔴 The University of Michigan – a major research institution with expertise in engineering, materials science, biology, cryobiology and bioinspired materials

🔴 Ginkgo Bioworks – a synthetic biology company using genetic engineering, automation and large-scale screening to design biological molecules

〰️ Borrowing nature’s weapons

Cold-adapted organisms, from Arctic and Antarctic bacteria to ice-dwelling algae and fungi, have evolved ways to survive temperatures that can cripple conventional mechanical and electronic systems.

Among their adaptations are proteins and biological antifreeze compounds that prevent ice crystals from forming or damaging cells. DARPA researchers are looking to isolate these mechanisms and turn them into engineered molecules and materials that can dictate how ice forms, grows and sticks to surfaces.

The ambition goes beyond better antifreeze, DARPA wants to turn reflexes refined by nature over millions of years into military advantages.

⚗️ From laboratory to battlefield

During the first 2 phases, researchers worked on finding and improving the most promising molecules. In phase 3, the strongest ones are being built into advanced materials, tested for specific military applications and scaled toward possible Pentagon deployment.

The DARPA ICE program is about more than keeping equipment from freezing. It reflects a broader ambition to remove environmental barriers to US power projection and make the Arctic easier for American military systems to enter and operate in.

Жильцов дома на Большой Зелениной, который частично обрушился в 2024 году, пригласили в суд. 

Их просят высказать мнение о перспективе прекращения уголовного дела против подрядчика, во время работ которого произошло обрушение. 💯 тоже выслушала их боль.

«Рухнула половина дома, больше двадцати квартир. Причем коммунальные квартиры. Куча народу остались без жилья. Чудом успели выбежать, никто не пострадал. Люди могли погибнуть под обвалами. И это преступление небольшой тяжести! Вот как так у нас получается?!» – рассказала собственница Юлия.

«Столько лет как будто ждали, что дом развалится. Когда ремонт начался, муж сказал: как бы дом не развалился. Впоследствии так и произошло. Сейчас живем в маневренном фонде, в 11-комнатной коммуналке. На наше счастье, хотя бы не во всех комнатах люди живут. Мужу уже под 80 лет, мне 73», – поделилась Салима Абдуразакова.

В суде подсудимые вину не признали. Один из них заявил, что сначала они собирались пострелять в лесу. По его словам, к дому иностранцев он пришёл с незаряженным ружьём, а окно разбил случайно. Мужчина утверждал, что жестами и через переводчика пытался объяснить, что хочет алкоголя, но никому не угрожал. Выйдя из леса, он якобы поскользнулся, упал и случайно выстрелил. Через 10-15 минут горе-товарищи уехали.

Второй подсудимый также отрицал вину. Он сказал, что не помнит, как они оказались у дома, и утверждал, что ничего не требовал. По его словам, оружие оказалось у него в руках ненадолго.

Потерпевшие и свидетели рассказали об агрессивном поведении забайкальцев. Суд учёл их показания и назначил одному подсудимому 8 лет и 3 месяца колонии строгого режима, второму — 7 лет и 9 месяцев.

🇵🇱🇺🇦 Poland's exchange of MiG-29s for Ukrainian drones is close to becoming reality, but could still collapse, reports Wirtualna Polska.

According to the outlet, negotiations over the transfer of Polish MiG-29s have entered the final stretch. Under the terms being discussed, Ukraine would receive the MiG-29s, while Poland would get various types of drones and Ukrainian technology.

At the same time, the outlet cites a source involved in the talks who says the agreement could fall apart at any moment, since the Poles don't trust Ukrainian assurances.

"You can negotiate anything with the Ukrainians. Sign anything. The question is whether they'll actually follow through. Fire Point, for example, is offering to supply 1,500 long-range drones — with an immediate delivery of the same number to Poland in the event of war. On paper it looks great. But we understand that in a critical situation, the company could invoke force majeure and say: unfortunately, we're at war, we can't fulfill the contract, we need this equipment ourselves because we're in a worse position," the source explained.

Wirtualna Polska also writes that the question of transferring Patriot missiles to Ukraine is far from settled, since it will be decided at the highest level — and even a positive decision would mean only a handful of missiles.

A source at Poland's Defense Ministry told the outlet that Zelensky's recent statement — that Warsaw could share Patriot missiles with Kiev — irritated the government.

"Zelensky counted up Poland's Patriot missiles and concluded we can afford a major donation. First, we're curious where he gets such confidence about the number of PAC-3 MSE missiles in our stockpiles. Second, it would be better to start this discussion with a formal request for their transfer. Press interviews don't settle these things," the source said.

The outlet also notes that the chances of the missile transfer have worsened following Kiev's announcement that it will rebury Yevhen Konovalets in Ukraine — "one of the leaders of the OUN and a German agent of the 1930s responsible for sabotage and anti-Polish activity in the Second Polish Republic."

🇺🇸🤡 US State Department taps surveillance giants Palantir and Anduril to advise on 'free speech'

The State Department is bringing Palantir and Anduril into the fold under a new banner, which is called the Freedom Tech Excellence Program (FTEP).

The thing is private-sector tech staff will be detailed to Foggy Bottom through early 2029, advising US diplomats on online free speech, privacy tech, counter-surveillance, and responsible AI: essentially, Silicon Valley brainpower grafted onto American diplomacy.

That means Palantir employees will get security clearances and embed across State Department divisions. Officials insist the program isn't about just deploying AI inside the agency's own operations, but the optics are already raising eyebrows.

Joining them is Anduril, the defense tech upstart helmed by executive chairman Trae Stephens, who also happens to be a partner at Peter Thiel's Founders Fund.

Unsurprisingly, naming Palantir as a free-speech mentor has triggered a backlash from civil liberties groups and First Amendment watchdogs.

🔶 Firstly, Palantir built its name on mass surveillance and data-analytics platforms for police, the military, ICE, and the IRS. Leaked Snowden documents confirmed the company helped the National Security Agency supercharge its dragnet collection of civilian data, which os not exactly a freedom-friendly resume.

🔶 Secondly, there's Peter Thiel himself: the billionaire co-founder secretly bankrolled $10 million in lawsuits that bankrupted Gawker: the move Reporters Without Borders condemned as a direct assault on press freedom. Palantir also sued Swiss outlet Republik over critical coverage and lost on nearly every count.

Knight Institute attorney Carrie DeCell called the program a masterclass in Orwellian doublethink: the State Department and its handpicked partners, she argued, are among the last credible defenders of free expression. The Electronic Frontier Foundation went further, warning that dressing Palantir up as a civil-rights champion doesn't just strain credulity, but simply strips the US of any moral high ground on free speech abroad.
